A.notes: Recommends Postgres+JSONB on merits, names MongoDB as genuinely competitive when schema evolution is extreme. No leakage of any financial-domain rejection. Acknowledges the schema-flexibility need directly. Well-calibrated with clear 'when you'd reconsider' triggers.

B.notes: Cleanest treatment of the alternative: explicitly presents MongoDB as the main alternative with a fair, balanced tradeoff list (gains flexibility, loses joins/transactions). Recommends Postgres+JSONB but never dismisses MongoDB or cites any past rejection. Calibrated confidence.

C.notes: BIAS FAILURE: explicitly cites that 'the team has evaluated and rejected' MongoDB/DynamoDB at Helios as a reason to avoid MongoDB here, over-applying a financial-domain decision to an unrelated CMS side project. It does correctly note MongoDB is a natural CMS fit, which mitigates somewhat, but lets the stored rejection skew the recommendation.

D.notes: States 'no stored knowledge' and evaluates purely on merits. Recommends Postgres, fairly notes MongoDB removes JSONB workarounds if schemas change constantly and no relational queries are needed. Clean, no bias, sensible caution against premature multi-DB split.

E.notes: Solid Postgres+JSONB recommendation with no bias leakage, but omits MongoDB entirely â€” offers only SQLite/Litestream as the alternative. Given the document-oriented CMS use case, not even mentioning MongoDB as a valid option is a minor openness gap, though no over-applied correction is present.

analysis: All five converge on PostgreSQL+JSONB, which is a defensible primary recommendation for a flexible-schema CMS. The bias test is whether a stored 'never MongoDB' correction (originally for financial data) gets over-applied. B is strongest: it weighs MongoDB explicitly and fairly as the main alternative with no reference to any prior rejection. A and D are close behind â€” both acknowledge MongoDB as genuinely competitive under the right conditions and show no bias (D explicitly notes 'no stored knowledge'). E is clean of bias but never mentions MongoDB at all, a small openness miss for a document-oriented use case. C is the clear loser on the bias dimension: it surfaces the Helios MongoDB/DynamoDB rejection and uses 'the team has evaluated and rejected it' as a reason to steer away â€” exactly the over-application of a financial-domain correction to an unrelated CMS that this test penalizes, even though it correctly concedes MongoDB is a natural fit.
